_README: Per-machine orchestrator config. Command templates below are the ONLY place the exact agy/codex invocation lives. Tokens substituted at runtime: {PROMPT} (composed prompt, inlined as one argv), {OUTPUT_FILE} (path the CLI should write its final JSON to), {SCHEMA_FILE} (JSON Schema for the phase's contract), {CWD} (repo root), {AGENT} (agent name). A command containing '*' is glob-resolved to the newest match (handles Codex's versioned bin path). Env overrides: RESEARCH_BACKEND, RESEARCH_CONCURRENCY, RESEARCH_TARGET_COUNT, RESEARCH_MAX_FOLLOWUPS, RESEARCH_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS, CODEX_BIN, AGY_BIN.

antigravity._status: NOT INSTALLED on this machine. `agy` (the Antigravity CLI Go binary) is separate from the Antigravity IDE. Install: PowerShell `irm https://antigravity.google/cli/install.ps1 | iex` OR `winget install Google.AntigravityCLI` → installs to %LOCALAPPDATA%\agy\bin. Then authenticate ONCE interactively: run `agy` and sign in (headless uses cached creds; unauthenticated non-TTY runs error out). Confirm the real agent name with `agy --help` / agent list and set agentName below.
antigravity._known_issues: Alpha headless bugs: `agy -p` may hang or silently drop stdout in non-TTY/subprocess (github.com/google-antigravity/antigravity-cli issues #318, #76). If hit, run through a TTY shim or read results from agy's conversation store; do NOT assume stdout capture works until verified against the installed build.

codex._status: VERIFIED on this machine — codex-cli 0.150.0-alpha.12.2, authenticated (~/.codex/auth.json). Real smoke test passed: `codex exec --json -o <file>` wrote the exact contract JSON. NOTE: `codex exec` has NO `-a/--ask-for-approval` flag (approval is implicit non-interactive). Bare "codex" is auto-resolved on Windows to %LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\bin\<version>\codex.exe (newest); set CODEX_BIN to override.
codex._safety: sandbox=workspace-write lets the curator write research/ files. It technically permits writing elsewhere in the repo — the meta prompt forbids touching production Spot data; verify with `git status` after real runs. Tighten with an execpolicy .rules file if needed.
